review_conclusions: Spools stay in memory at exactly64KiB and spill only when a subsequent write makes the length exceed that threshold. The shared attempt allocates its directory lazily and enforces its cumulative spill-file count before directory/file allocation.

The attempt journal carries magic/version/process/attempt identifiers. Journal initialization failure attempts directory rollback; Drop paths close owned file handles and perform best-effort file/directory cleanup.

Only serialize_to_spool fills accounted_bytes with the shared document-budget delta. Other wrapper spools retain zero; duplicate-key replacement refunds the previous serialized value delta, while copied bytes use preaccounted output and temporary work remains cumulative.

The map-key serializer accepts supported scalar spellings, recursively unwraps Some and ordinary newtypes, and rejects null/unit/bytes/composite/RawValue forms. Integer macro methods, finite numeric keys and all Impossible container types were traced.

Map-key encoded length includes quotes, UTF-8 bytes and exact JSON escapes. The length helper and string writer agree on quote/backslash/common controls and the remaining U+0000..001F six-byte escapes.

Display adapters preserve a concrete budget/I/O error outside fmt::Error; a formatter's own rejection maps to payload validation. The preaccounted string entry requires the caller to reserve the full encoded key size.
